beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:hushed wonder, the legend]An island ^empire, rich and proud. [act:slow, ominous but calm][tune:fall]Swallowed by the ^sea, in a ^single day and night.

[d:tension][act:leaning in, the catch][tune:fall]It is the most famous lost city on Earth. [act:leaning in, the catch][tune:fall]And only ^one person ever wrote it down. [act:dry, letting it land][tune:fall]^Nine thousand years after it supposedly ^sank.

[d:calm][act:setting the scene, measured][tune:level]That person is ^Plato, the Greek philosopher, around {360|three sixty} BCE. [p:0.93][act:reporting his claim, neutral]In two of his written dialogues, he says the story came from ^Egyptian priests, through the lawgiver ^Solon: passed along like a message, hand to ^hand. [go:1|0][act:plain fact, a little weight][tune:fall]But no ^older text has ever been found, in Egypt or in Greece. [act:quiet, firm][tune:highfall]Not ^one.

[d:build][act:conspiratorial, drawing closer][tune:fall]But here's the ^strange part. [p:0.93][act:careful, precise][tune:fall]Plato puts the war with Atlantis nine thousand years before Solon: about {9600|ninety-six hundred} BCE.

[d:build][sfx:shimmer][act:the evidence, steady and clear][tune:fall]Now, geologists date the end of the last Ice Age cold snap to about {9700|ninety-seven hundred} BCE. [p:0.93][act:explaining, a simple picture]Polar ice piles up year after year, like pages in a ^diary, and each page records@verb how cold that year ^was. [act:brisk, vivid][tune:fall]As the ice melted, the seas were rising ^fast. [act:genuinely intrigued, slower][tune:fall]Only a century apart. [act:genuinely intrigued, slower][tune:fall]That ^is a strange match.

[d:build][act:changing scene, brisk][tune:fall]Now the ^ocean. [act:explaining, clear and patient]Beyond Gibraltar, the sea floor is ^young volcanic rock, still ^spreading from a ridge down the middle of the Atlantic. [p:0.93][act:explaining, a simple picture]Lava wells up at the ridge, cools into new floor, and is pushed aside, like two conveyor belts running ^apart.

[d:build][act:plain, firm][tune:fall]There's ^no sunken continent down there: no room to ^hide one. [act:widening the lens, measured][tune:fall]And ^nowhere on Earth, at that date, is there a ^bronze-working empire with ships. [act:plain, explaining]People worked ^stone, not metal. [act:plain, explaining][tune:fall]Bronze came some six thousand years ^later.

[d:reveal][act:the reveal, lean in][tune:fall]And Plato didn't need to ^invent a drowning. [sfx:hit][act:vivid, telling it straight]In {373|three seventy-three} BCE, an ^earthquake and a wave swallowed the Greek city of ^Helike. [act:quiet, pointed][tune:fall]Plato was ^alive at the time. [act:a knowing nod][tune:fall]He'd have ^heard the news.
[d:aside][act:wry, a small smile][tune:fall]A real city, swallowed by a real ^sea. [act:wry, a small smile][tune:fall]Sometimes the ^news writes the myth.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm authority][tune:rise]A sunken Atlantic ^empire? [act:the verdict, level-headed][tune:fall]*Ruled ^out*. [act:lighter, one eyebrow up][tune:rise]The ^date? [act:fair-minded, even][tune:fall]A ^coincidence worth ^noticing. [p:0.93][act:fair, explaining]Two dates that line up are a ^clue to check, not an ^answer.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:balanced, sincere][tune:fall]The story is ^Plato's. [act:the last word, quiet and sure][tune:fall]The rising ^seas were ^real.
